newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian "closed" carpet firm opens up to public.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian "closed" carpet firm opens up to public.

text.p: Egypt's privately owned Oriental Weavers/Carpet Factory on Saturday offered shares to the public to raise its capital, in a rare offering by one of the country's "closed" firms.
A closed firm in Egypt is one that is registered on the bourse but whose shares are held by a small number of private investors who rarely trade them. Such firms are usually owned by families.

Individuals must buy a minimum of 50 shares at 58.4 pounds ($17.20) a share, plus an issuance fee of 0.25 pounds, the company said in a published announcement. The share last traded on February 26 at 105 pounds.
The firm said it would issue 2.5 million shares, at a nominal value of 10 pounds a share, to increase the issued capital to 135 million pounds from 110 million.
The offer will open for two months from May 25. It can be closed, however, after a minimum statutory period of 10 days.

"The company occupies a leading place in the world industry of machine-made carpets and world demand for its products has increased...It has embarked on an expansion project, of which the first phase will complete in 1997," the firm said.
The forecast return on capital is 12 percent, it added.
Oriental Weavers is among well-performing firms in Egypt's manufacturing sector.
Its gross profits rose to 48.324 million pounds in 1996 from 36.807 million in the previous year. They are forecast to more than double to 76.025 million in 1997 and 87.998 million in 1998.
Shareholders' funds also rose to 133.032 million pounds at the end of April 1997 from 97.381 million at the end of financial year 1996.
Pre-tax profits are forecast to also double to 63.693 million pounds in 1997 from 28.707 million in 1996.
The firm is majority-owned by the chairman of the Industries Federation, Mohamed Farid Khamis, who holds 62.68 percent. Khamis is among prominent industrialists in Egypt.
The state banks National Bank of Egypt and Suez Canal Bank, and the brokerage firm Egyptian Anglo for Financial Investments are handling the offer.
In January, Cairo Precision became one of the first Egyptian "closed" companies to open up to the public through a share issue.
